messages:
maria-support: Hey team, customer ACME Corp opened an escalation — calls to /v1/generate are intermittently hitting us from eu-west but their org is pinned to us-east. Seeing huge latency spikes and 401s. Can someone take a look?

nate-eng-oncall: On it. Do we have a sample request id or curl? Also which gateway cluster is fronting their tenant?

maria-support: Request IDs: req=01H4X2A9QZ0T1KZ3P4Y, req=01H4X2B0RZ0T1KZ3P7A. Customer notes this started ~2026-03-17T14:20Z. Account org_id=acme-corp-42. They say they pinned model routing to us-east and set region_hint header.

jamie-platops: Reproduced quickly from my laptop with org header. curl: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -H "X-Redwood-Org: acme-corp-42" -H "X-Region-Hint: us-east-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response has 200 occasionally, but many 401/504 and some 200s with header `x-served-region: eu-west-1`.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout of gateway v2.14 started at 2026-03-17T13:58Z across eu-west and us-west pools.

nate-eng-oncall: That deploy could be related. Jamie, can you paste the full response headers when the 401 occurs? Also check for `x-original-region` / `x-proxy-region` headers.

jamie-platops: Example failing response headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
content-type: application/json
x-served-region: eu-west-1
x-original-host: gateway-internal.eu-west.pool
x-request-id: 01H4X2A9QZ0T1KZ3P4Y
```
Body: `{ "error": "invalid token for org" }`

elie-rtg: That x-served-region is wrong. If the request is routed to eu-west, token issuer check fails because auth keys are per-region and the token is scoped to us-east KMS. Shouldn't the smart router respect tenant pinning?

nate-eng-oncall: I'm pulling routing logs. Looks like L7 header-based route selection uses `X-Region-Hint` but fallback policy allows cross-region if local capacity < 10% threshold. Canary added a change to compute capacity using node-level slots and a race condition could mis-evaluate pool capacity — causing fallback to eu-west.

maria-support: Customer is seeing billing breaks too — tokens counted in eu-west metrics, which their cost center doesn't expect. They want immediate mitigation.

nate-eng-oncall: Mitigation options: 1) Roll back gateway v2.14 canary to stop new misroutes, 2) Add immediate header rewrite in front of envoy to enforce X-Region-Hint -> x-served-region mapping, 3) Temporarily tighten fallback so pinned orgs never leave their region. Which do we want now?

jamie-platops: Rolling back is fastest. I'll coordinate with eng-releases. But we should also patch envoy route: there's a bug where `x-original-host` header is preserved incorrectly across internal redirects, and the L7 policy checks `host` first then header. We can add a short-term lua filter to normalize region header.

kube-bot: kube: Rolling restart of gateway-canary pods in eu-west initiated by jamie-platops at 2026-03-17T14:32Z.

nate-eng-oncall: Patch plan: jamie to apply lua header normalize -> set `x-served-region` from `X-Region-Hint` if present, and short-circuit fallback for orgs with `X-Redwood-Org` in pinned list. I'll prepare a follow-up hotfix for the capacity calc race.

jamie-platops: Pushed lua filter to canary. Quick smoke: repeated curl now shows `x-served-region: us-east-1` consistently. No more 401s in my 20 tries.

maria-support: Customer confirmed reduced latency and auth success in their last check (they reported 200s now). They're asking for an RCA and whether any data left the region.

nate-eng-oncall: Short answer: no user data processed in eu-west for acme-corp-42 beyond initial misrouted requests (we're verifying logs for token validation failures only). We'll produce full RCA: root cause = gateway v2.14 canary introduced race in capacity health calculation + envoy header preservation bug. Immediate fix = lua filter + rollback of canary to stop new misroutes, long-term fix = capacity calc rewrite + add unit/integration tests around header invariants.

elie-rtg: Also adding perf regression check: any requests that hit eu-west will have higher latency and could affect SLA. We should backfill metrics and tag customer traces as impacted.

maria-support: I'll open a postmortem ticket and notify account team. ACME wants credits for the window 14:20Z-14:34Z.

nate-eng-oncall: Filed incident IR-2026-03-17-02 and assigned to eng-runtime. Next actions: eng-releases rollback audit, runtime capacity patch, and security confirm no key exfiltration. I'll update thread when RCA draft is ready.

jamie-platops: Rollback completed at 2026-03-17T14:40Z. Canary traffic moved back to v2.13; lua filter left in place as a short-lived guard.

maria-support: Thanks — I'll close the support escalation once RCA & credit plan confirmed. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident-bot: IR-2026-03-17-02 created, severity P2, link: https://incidents.redwood.ai/IR-2026-03-17-02
